prompt: I'm a software engineer, mid-30s. I've been coding professionally for 10+ years, mostly Python and distributed systems stuff. I took calculus in college but honestly barely remember anything beyond basic derivatives. I've never formally studied linear algebra and it's biting me now — I'm trying to get more into ML/AI work, and every time I read a paper the math section stops me cold. Matrix operations, SVD, eigenvectors, that whole world. I want to get to the point where I can read an ML paper and actually follow the math, and where I know what I'm doing when I write numpy code instead of just copying from stackoverflow. I can commit about 45 minutes on weekdays, maybe a bit more on weekends. No hard deadline but I'd like to feel real progress within a month or two. Where do I start and what should my plan look like?

assertions.text: Includes a concrete daily session structure with time allocations (minutes per activity)
Includes a phased roadmap with named milestones and approximate timelines
Explicitly prioritizes active problem-solving / production over passive consumption
Includes spaced / distributed review of previously-learned material
Includes interleaved or mixed-practice review drawing from multiple past topics
Includes retrieval-based practice or self-quizzing without looking at notes
Requires mastery of prerequisites before advancing (not moving on from 'kinda getting it')
Names specific resources (textbooks, videos, tools) rather than vague pointers
Warns that the plan will feel slower/harder than intuitive study methods (desirable difficulty)
Names specific anti-patterns or failure modes tailored to this learner
Recommends a problem-heavy primary resource (ideally a textbook like Strang) and flags video-first as insufficient
References eigenvalues/SVD as target-level topics the plan should reach
Names at least one explicit accountability mechanism (tutor, study partner, public commitment, forcing function, streak, etc.)
Specifies pivot signals — explicit conditions that, if they occur, would mean the plan needs adjustment
